questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
When a homeowner became ill, he properly executed a deed sufficient to convey his home to his nephew, who was then serving overseas in the military. Two persons signed as witnesses to qualify the deed for recording under an applicable statute. The homeowner handed the deed to his nephew's friend and said to her, "I want [the nephew] to have my home. Please take this deed for him." Shortly thereafter, the nephew's friend learned that the homeowner's death was imminent. One day before the homeowner's death, the nephew's friend recorded the deed. The nephew returned home shortly after the homeowner's death, learned about the deed, and took possession of the home. The homeowner had died intestate, leaving a daughter as his sole heir. When she asserted ownership of the home, the nephew brought an appropriate action against her to determine title. The law of the jurisdiction requires only two witnesses for a will to be properly executed.
If the court rules for the nephew and against the daughter, what will be the most likely explanation?

choices.A: The deed was delivered when the homeowner handed it to the nephew's friend.
choices.B: The delivery of the deed was accomplished by the recording of the deed.
choices.C: The homeowner's death consummated a valid gift causa mortis to the nephew.
choices.D: The homeowner's properly executed deed was effective as a testamentary document.

questions.explanation:
Presumptive delivery of a deed

A deed is a legal instrument that transfers ownership of real property from the owner (grantor) to another (grantee). But to be effective, the deed must be:

  • delivered by the grantor – evidenced by the grantor's present intent to convey ownership to the grantee and
  • accepted by the grantee – presumed if the transfer is beneficial to the grantee.

Delivery is presumed when the deed has been recorded or is in the grantee's possession. Delivery also occurs when the deed is physically handed to the grantee's agent—i.e., a third party acting on behalf of the grantee.

Here, the homeowner properly executed a deed conveying his home to the nephew. Since that transfer benefited the nephew, acceptance is presumed. Therefore, if the court rules in favor of the nephew, the most likely explanation is that the deed was delivered when the homeowner handed it to the nephew's friend (agent) and told her to take it on the nephew's behalf.

(Choice B) Recording a deed (ie, filing it in official land records) creates a presumption of delivery. But here, delivery occurred when the homeowner handed the deed to the nephew's friend before the deed was recorded.

(Choice C) A gift causa mortis (ie, deathbed gift) is a gift of personal property made in expectation of the grantor's imminent death. Here, the homeowner gifted real property (his home) to the nephew. And this gift was not made in expectation of imminent death since the homeowner's death became imminent after he delivered the deed.

(Choice D) A deed requires the grantor's present intent to convey ownership to the grantee—ie, the grantor must intend that title transfer immediately. And since a testamentary document (eg, a will or testament) only takes effect upon the testator's death (no intent to presently transfer), a deed cannot serve as a testamentary document.

📌 Educational Objective

To effectively transfer an interest in real property, a deed must be (1) delivered by the grantor and (2) accepted by the grantee. The grantor can deliver the deed by handing it to the grantee's agent.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Property: Donative Transfers § 32.3 (Am. Law Inst. 1992) (transfer relating to land).
questions.zh-question:
一位房主生病后，妥善签署了一份足以将其房屋转让给当时正在海外服兵役的侄子的地契。根据适用的法规，有两人作为见证人签署，使该地契具备了登记资格。房主将地契交给了侄子的朋友，并对她说：“我希望[侄子]拥有我的房子。请为了他收下这份地契。”此后不久，侄子的朋友得知房主即将去世。在房主去世的前一天，侄子的朋友登记了该地契。房主去世后不久，侄子回到家中，得知了地契的事情，并占有了该房屋。房主无遗嘱死亡，留下一个女儿作为其唯一继承人。当女儿主张对房屋的所有权时，侄子对她提起了适当的诉讼以确定所有权。该司法管辖区的法律规定，一份有效订立的遗嘱仅需两名见证人。

如果法院作出有利于侄子而不利于女儿的裁决，最可能的解释是什么？

zh-choices.A: 当房主将地契交给侄子的朋友时，地契即已交付。
zh-choices.B: 地契的交付是通过地契的登记完成的。
zh-choices.C: 房主的死亡促成了一项对侄子的有效的临终赠与（gift causa mortis）。
zh-choices.D: 房主妥善签署的地契作为一份遗嘱文件是有效的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Titles - Delivery and Recording of Deed

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：契据（deed）是不是已经通过交付生效，尤其是交给受赠人朋友这种 受赠人代理人（grantee's agent） 的交付算不算数。

三秒认题路径：

已执行契据 → 交给朋友 → 表示给侄子 → 记录前已交付 → 选 A

核心法律规则

不动产的 契据（deed） 要有效，必须有 交付（delivery） 和 接受（acceptance）。交付 看的是让渡人现在就想把产权转出去的意思，不是等死后才生效。

如果契据被记录，或已经落到受赠人手里，通常会推定已经交付；更重要的是，把契据交给 受赠人代理人（grantee's agent） 也算交付，所以这题里真正锁定答案的是“交给侄子的朋友，让她替侄子拿着”。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用于本题；本题锁定的是不动产契据交付规则：交给受赠人代理人即可成立交付。

思维导图

题干先问：这份 契据（deed） 什么时候已经生效？
关卡 1：有没有 交付（delivery）？
看事实：屋主把契据交给侄子的朋友，还说“请替他拿着”。
这一步已经是交给 受赠人代理人（grantee's agent），交付成立。
关卡 2：记录（recording）只是辅助推定，不是唯一生效方式。
本题杀点：在记录之前，交付就已经完成，所以不用靠记录补救。
关卡 3：不是 临终赠与（gift causa mortis）。
原因：这送的是房子，属于不动产，不是个人财产。
结论：交付已成，侄子取得产权，答案到 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是 recorded 之后才大家都看得见，那应该是记录才让契据生效。

但考试真正问的是：交付先发生还是后发生；本题在记录前就已经把契据交给侄子的朋友了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干关键事实是屋主把 deed 交给侄子的朋友并说明要给侄子，这就是对受赠人代理人的交付；因为对侄子有利，接受也推定成立。

❌ 事实误判 | 记录时点偷换

✕ B: 把 recording 当成唯一生效点，忽略更早的交付。

❌ 法律适用 | 临终赠与错套

✕ C: 硬套 gift causa mortis，但这题是房产契据，不是个人财产赠与。

❌ 概念混淆 | 遗嘱功能乱配

✕ D: 把 testamentary 当成契据功能，但契据要求的是现在转让，不是死后才生效。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“交付给谁”，再看是否已交给受赠人代理人；记录只会加分，不是唯一入口。

考场速记

记忆口诀：契据要交付，交给代理人也算交付；先看有没有现在转让的意思，再看记录只是推定。

reason.en: Establishes the instrument was capable of transferring title if delivered and accepted.
reason.zh: 表明该文书在交付并被接受后即可转移产权。

keywords.text: handed the deed to his nephew's friend

reason.en: The handoff is the key act that may constitute delivery to the grantee through an agent.
reason.zh: 该交付行为可能是通过代理人向受让人完成契据交付的关键。

keywords.text: Please take this deed for him

reason.en: Shows present intent to convey to the nephew and authorizes the friend to act as his agent.
reason.zh: 表明向侄子现时转让的意图，并授权朋友作为其代理人。

reason.en: Explains why delivery through a friend rather than directly to the nephew was necessary.
reason.zh: 说明为何需要通过朋友而非直接向侄子交付。

reason.en: Recording may create a presumption of delivery but does not necessarily mark the first delivery.
reason.zh: 登记可产生交付推定，但未必是首次交付时点。

reason.en: Creates competing claim by the heir if the deed was not effectively delivered before death.
reason.zh: 若死亡前契据未有效交付，则继承人可主张 competing ownership。

keywords.text: requires only two witnesses for a will

reason.en: Distracts by invoking will formalities that do not govern deed delivery.
reason.zh: 以遗嘱形式要件干扰，与契据交付规则无关。

reason.en: States the correct doctrine that title transfer requires grantor delivery.
reason.zh: 指出产权转移需 grantor 交付的正确规则。

A.text: handed it to the nephew's friend

reason.en: Identifies the moment and method of delivery that supports the nephew's title.
reason.zh: 指出支持侄子取得产权的交付时点与方式。

B.text: accomplished by the recording of the deed

reason.en: Misplaces delivery at recording when handoff to the agent already occurred.
reason.zh: 将交付时点误置于登记，忽略此前向代理人交付。

reason.en: Recording only raises a presumption and is not the only delivery mechanism here.
reason.zh: 登记仅产生推定，并非本案唯一交付方式。

reason.en: Applies a personal-property gift rule to real property and wrong timing.
reason.zh: 将动产临终赠与规则错误适用于不动产且时点不符。

reason.en: Treats death as consummating transfer rather than deed delivery before death.
reason.zh: 误以死亡完成转让，而非死亡前的契据交付。

reason.en: Confuses a deed requiring present transfer with a will effective only at death.
reason.zh: 混淆需现时转让的契据与仅在死亡时生效的遗嘱。

reason.en: Proper execution alone does not make a deed testamentary or delay transfer until death.
reason.zh: 有效签署本身不能使契据成为遗嘱或延迟至死亡时转让。

highlights.text: handed the deed to his nephew's friend and said to her, "I want [the nephew] to have my home. Please take this deed for him."

reason.en: This language shows present intent to convey and delivery through the nephew's agent.
reason.zh: 该表述显示现时转让意图，并通过侄子代理人完成交付。

highlights.text: One day before the homeowner's death, the nephew's friend recorded the deed.

reason.en: Tempts test-takers to treat recording, not the earlier handoff, as delivery.
reason.zh: 易诱使考生将登记而非更早的交付视为交付时点。

highlights.text: properly executed a deed sufficient to convey his home to his nephew

reason.en: Confirms the deed was valid on its face if delivery and acceptance occurred.
reason.zh: 确认契据本身有效，关键在于是否完成交付与接受。

highlights.text: The law of the jurisdiction requires only two witnesses for a will to be properly executed.

reason.en: Distracts from deed delivery by suggesting will-execution rules control the outcome.
reason.zh: 以遗嘱签署规则干扰，与契据交付争点无关。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An aunt owned a large parcel of vacant land in fee simple and executed a deed purporting to convey the land to her nephew. She told her nephew, who was then 19, about the deed and said that she would give it to him when he reached 21 and had received his undergraduate college degree. Shortly afterward the nephew searched his aunt's desk, found and removed the deed, and recorded it.
A month later, the nephew executed an instrument in the proper form of a warranty deed purporting to convey the land to his fiancée. He delivered the deed to his fiancée, pointing out that the deed recited that it was given in exchange for "$1 and other good and valuable consideration," and that to make it valid his fiancée must pay him $1. The fiancée, impressed and grateful, did so. Together, they went to the recording office and recorded the deed. The fiancée assumed that the nephew had owned the land and knew nothing about the nephew's dealing with his aunt. Neither the aunt's deed to the nephew nor the nephew's deed to the fiancée said anything about any conditions.
The recording act of the jurisdiction provides: "No conveyance or mortgage of real property shall be good against subsequent purchasers for value and without notice unless the same be recorded according to law."
Two years passed. The nephew turned 21, then graduated from college. At the graduation party, the aunt was chatting with the fiancée and for the first time learned the foregoing facts.
The age of majority in the jurisdiction is 18 years.
If the aunt brings an appropriate action against the fiancée to quiet title to the land, who will prevail?

choices.A: The aunt, because her deed to the nephew was not delivered.
choices.B: The aunt, because her nephew's deed to his fiancée before the nephew satisfied the aunt's conditions was void, as the fiancée had paid only nominal consideration.
choices.C: The fiancée, because the deed to her was recorded.
choices.D: The fiancée, because the nephew has satisfied the aunt's oral conditions.

Aunt prevails

A deed is a legal instrument that transfers ownership of real property from the grantor (old owner) to a grantee (new owner) once it has been:

  • delivered - evidenced by the grantor's intent to presently convey ownership to the grantee (ie, conditional deliveries are ineffective) and
  • accepted - presumed when the transfer is beneficial to the grantee.

Delivery is presumed if the deed is recorded (ie, filed in official land records). But this presumption can be rebutted by evidence that the grantor did not intend to presently transfer ownership. And if a deed is not delivered (and accepted), it is void and conveys no interest—not even to a bona fide purchaser.

Here, the nephew and fiancée recorded the deed (presumed delivery). But that presumption is rebuttable since the aunt had placed the deed in a drawer and told the nephew it would be his when he reached 21 and graduated (conditional delivery). Since she did not intend to presently transfer ownership to the nephew, the deed was not delivered and conveyed no interest to the nephew. Therefore, his subsequent conveyance to the fiancée was ineffective (even though she was a bona fide purchaser), and the aunt will prevail.

(Choice B) The deed is void because it was never delivered. But had the aunt delivered the deed, the nephew could have conveyed his interest in the property before it became possessory—ie, before he satisfied the aunt's conditions. And the fiancée's payment of only nominal consideration ($1) would have been inconsequential since consideration is not required to convey property through a deed.

(Choice C) Although the deed from the nephew to the fiancée was recorded, he had no property interest to convey to her since the aunt's prior deed had not been delivered to him. Therefore, ownership never transferred to the nephew or the fiancée.

(Choice D) Although the nephew met the aunt's oral conditions (he turned 21 and graduated from college), the deed was never delivered. Therefore, the nephew had no property interest to give the fiancée.

📌 Educational Objective

A deed transfers ownership of real property once it is delivered (when the grantor has an intent to presently convey ownership) and accepted (presumed when the transfer is beneficial to the grantee). An undelivered or unaccepted deed is void and conveys no property interest to the grantee.
questions.zh-question:
一位姑母以完全所有权（fee simple）的形式拥有一大片空地，并签署了一份旨在将该土地转让给其侄子的地契。她告诉当时19岁的侄子关于这份地契的事，并说当他年满21岁并获得大学本科学位时，她会把地契交给他。不久之后，侄子搜查了他姑母的书桌，找到并拿走了地契，并将其登记备案。

一个月后，侄子以担保地契（warranty deed）的适当形式签署了一份文书，旨在将该土地转让给他的未婚妻。他将地契交付给他的未婚妻，并指出地契上记载该地契是为交换“1美元及其他有益和有价的对价（consideration）”而授予的，并且为了使其有效，他的未婚妻必须支付他1美元。未婚妻深受感动并心怀感激，照做了。他们一起去了登记处，将地契登记备案。未婚妻想当然地认为侄子拥有该土地，并且对侄子与他姑母之间的事一无所知。姑母给侄子的地契和侄子给未婚妻的地契均未提及任何条件。

该司法管辖区的登记法案规定：“任何不动产的转让或抵押，除非依法登记，否则不得对抗后续的有偿且无通知的购买者。”

两年过去了。侄子年满21岁，然后大学毕业。在毕业派对上，姑母与未婚妻聊天时，才首次得知上述事实。

该司法管辖区的成年年龄为18岁。

如果姑母对未婚妻提起适当的诉讼以明晰该土地的产权（quiet title），谁将胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 姑母，因为她给侄子的地契并未交付。
zh-choices.B: 姑母，因为在侄子满足姑母的条件之前，他给未婚妻的地契是无效的，因为未婚妻仅支付了名义上的对价。
zh-choices.C: 未婚妻，因为给她的地契已经登记备案。
zh-choices.D: 未婚妻，因为侄子已经满足了姑母的口头条件。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Titles - Titles

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：契据（deed）有没有完成交付（delivery）；没交付就不转移产权，后面再录、再转都救不回来。

三秒认题路径：

先看交付 → 再看意图 → 录了也不等于交付 → 后手无权可转 → 所以选房东

核心法律规则

这题只看一件事：契据有没有真正交付

交付（delivery）的考场意思是：出让人现在就想把所有权交出去，不是“以后条件满足再说”。如果只是附条件交付（conditional delivery），而且条件还没成，契据就没有生效。

录入登记（recording）在这里最多只会制造“好像已经交付”的推定，但这个推定可以被原始事实推翻。没有交付，就没有产权；没有产权，后面的买受人就算善意、给价、还登记，也拿不到东西。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题不是上诉，而是看 deed 是否已经 delivery。

思维导图

姑妈 保留控制权
→
契据放抽屉 只说以后再给
→
未交付 产权没出去
→
侄子偷走并登记 只能制造推定
→
侄子再转给未婚妻 下游也拿不到产权
→
姑妈 quiet title 胜 无权转让，后手落空

考点陷阱

你可能会想：侄子后来已经满 21 岁、也毕业了，好像条件都满足了，未婚妻又登记了，应该能保住产权。

但考试真正问的是：当时有没有交付，不是后来条件有没有凑齐。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里同样是看产权有没有先从姑妈手里出去；没有出去，后面一切都只是空转。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里姑妈只说“等到 21 岁并毕业再给”，这是 条件性保留，说明她没有立刻交付；所以契据没生效，侄子和未婚妻都拿不到产权。

❌ 概念混淆 | 价金误判

✕ B: 把 nominal consideration 当成关键，但这题输赢不看 1 美元，看有没有交付。

❌ 法律适用 | 登记优先误判

✕ C: 只盯着 recorded，却忘了前手没交付，后手登记也救不活空权利。

❌ 事实误判 | 条件成就误判

✕ D: 把后来成年毕业当成转移完成，但契据早就没交付，事后补不回产权。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定 交付，再看登记和善意买受人；前手没权，后手就没有可继受的产权。

考场速记

记住一句：deed 先看 delivery，再看 recording；没交付，就算录了也只是“假象”，产权不会自动飞出去。

这题的快捷键就是：先问“现在转没转”，别被“以后满足条件”带偏。

reason.en: Starts the chain of title transfers that must be validly delivered.
reason.zh: 开启须有效交付的产权转让链条。

keywords.text: when he reached 21 and had received his undergraduate college degree

reason.en: Shows the aunt intended a future, not present, transfer to the nephew.
reason.zh: 表明阿姨意图在未来而非当下转让。

keywords.text: found and removed the deed, and recorded it

reason.en: Nephew's recording triggers only a rebuttable delivery presumption.
reason.zh: 侄子登记仅产生可推翻的交付推定。

keywords.text: purchasers for value and without notice

reason.en: Defines who the recording act protects if prior conveyances are valid.
reason.zh: 界定在前手转让有效时登记法保护的对象。

reason.en: Identifies the dispute as competing claims to ownership.
reason.zh: 表明争议在于 competing ownership claims。

keywords.text: Neither the aunt's deed to the nephew nor the nephew's deed to the fiancée said anything about any conditions

reason.en: Extrinsic evidence can rebut delivery despite silence in the instrument.
reason.zh: 契据未写条件时，外在证据仍可推翻交付。

A.text: her deed to the nephew was not delivered

reason.en: States the controlling defect preventing any transfer from the aunt.
reason.zh: 指出阻止阿姨转让生效的核心瑕疵。

B.text: before the nephew satisfied the aunt's conditions was void

reason.en: Misframes the problem as voidability for timing rather than lack of delivery.
reason.zh: 将问题误定为时机导致无效，而非未交付。

reason.en: Distracts with consideration law even though deeds need no consideration.
reason.zh: 用对价规则干扰，但契据转让无需对价。

C.text: because the deed to her was recorded

reason.en: Confuses recording-act protection with title where the grantor never delivered.
reason.zh: 混淆登记法保护与 grantor 从未交付时的产权。

D.text: because the nephew has satisfied the aunt's oral conditions

reason.en: Treats later fulfillment as curing a deed that was never delivered.
reason.zh: 误以为事后满足条件可补正从未交付的契据。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
Seven years ago, a man conveyed vacant land by warranty deed to a woman, a bona fide purchaser for value. The woman did not record the warranty deed and did not enter into possession of the land.
Five years ago, the man conveyed the same land to a neighbor, also a bona fide purchaser for value, by a quitclaim deed. The neighbor immediately recorded the quitclaim deed and went into possession of the land.
Two years ago, the neighbor conveyed the land to a friend, who had notice of the prior conveyance from the man to the woman. The friend never recorded the deed, but he went into immediate possession of the land.
The jurisdiction has a notice recording statute and a grantor-grantee index system.
If the woman sues to eject the friend, will the woman be likely to succeed?

choices.A: No, because the friend took possession of the land before the woman did.
choices.B: No, because the neighbor's title was superior to the woman's title.
choices.C: Yes, because the friend had notice of the conveyance from the man to the woman.
choices.D: Yes, because the woman, unlike the friend, took title under a warranty deed.

questions.explanation:
Shelter rule
Man owns vacant land
→
Man conveys land to woman
→
Man conveys same land to neighbor (BFP)
→
Neighbor sells land to friend (not BFP)
Priority over woman
Priority over woman

Recording acts are used to evaluate the priority of competing interests in the same property. Most recording acts protect bona fide purchasers (BFPs)—ie, persons who:

  • pay value for an interest in property and
  • lack notice of a prior interest.

In a jurisdiction with a notice recording act (as seen here), a BFP's property interest is always superior to an earlier competing property interest. And under the Shelter Rule, a person who receives a property interest from a BFP is protected from prior interests by the recording act to the same extent as the BFP.

Here, the man first conveyed the vacant land to the woman (BFP) and then conveyed it to the neighbor (BFP). Since the neighbor was a BFP, the neighbor's title was superior to the woman's earlier title under the notice statute. And though the friend knew about the earlier conveyance when the neighbor conveyed the land to him (not a BFP), he is sheltered by the neighbor's BFP status (Choice C). As a result, the woman will likely lose her suit to eject (ie, remove) the friend from the land.

(Choice A) The priority of competing property interests is not determined by who took possession first. Therefore, the friend's prior possession is not the reason the woman will lose. Instead, she will lose because the neighbor was a BFP and the friend is protected by the neighbor's BFP status under the Shelter Rule.

(Choice D) A warranty deed, unlike a quitclaim deed, contains assurances regarding the quality of title conveyed. But the type of deed is irrelevant in determining priority among competing property interests. Therefore, the fact that the woman took title under a warranty deed is not a basis for her to succeed in her suit to eject the friend.

📌 Educational Objective

In a notice jurisdiction, a bona fide purchaser (BFP) without notice of an earlier competing property interest has priority over that competing interest. And under the Shelter Rule, a person who receives a property interest from a BFP is protected from prior interests to the same extent as the BFP.

两年前，该邻居将土地转让给一位朋友，该朋友知悉之前男子向女性转让土地一事。该朋友从未登记该契约，但他立即占有了该土地。

该司法管辖区采用通知型登记法规和转让人-受让人索引系统。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Titles - Titles

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：在通知登记法（notice recording act）下，后手买到的人如果来自一个善意购买人（bona fide purchaser, BFP），会不会被庇护规则（shelter rule）带着一起“躲开”更早的权利人。

三秒认题路径：

先看是否BFP → 再看是否通知法 → 再看庇护规则 → 先买的人输

核心法律规则

通知登记法（notice recording act）的考场意思：后买的人只要是善意购买人（BFP），而且对先前权利没有通知（no notice），就能压过更早但没保护住的权利人。

庇护规则（shelter rule）的考场意思：从BFP手里拿到产权的人，即使自己知道旧权利，也能“借到”BFP的保护，所以通常仍可对抗旧权利人。

核心判例： 本题对应的核心逻辑就是shelter rule：邻居既然是BFP，朋友就能继承这层保护，即使朋友自己有通知也一样。

思维导图

先问：邻居从男人那里拿到时，自己的标题有没有压过女人？
有。 邻居是BFP，又先登记、先占有；在通知登记法（notice recording act）下，他的标题先赢女人。
卡死点：女人先拿到，不等于她先赢；这里真正决定胜负的是“邻居是不是BFP”。
再问：朋友明知旧转让，还能不能拿到保护？
能。 朋友虽然不是BFP，但他从BFP邻居手里受让，直接吃到庇护规则（shelter rule）。
卡死点：朋友的notice不重要，因为他是在“继承”邻居的BFP地位。
结论：女人能赶走朋友吗？
不能。 邻居标题先于女人，朋友又被庇护规则保护，所以女人起诉驱逐失败。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：朋友知道先前转让，怎么还能赢？

但考试真正问的是：朋友是不是从一个已经赢过女人的BFP那里拿权利。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干里邻居是BFP，在通知登记法下已经压过女人；朋友再从邻居受让时，又被庇护规则带着一起赢，所以女人不能驱逐他。

❌ 事实误判 | 先占混淆

✕ A: 把possession当成优先顺序标准了。

❌ 法律适用 | 忽略庇护

✕ C: 只盯着朋友有通知，漏掉他是从BFP邻居手里拿权利。

❌ 概念混淆 | 契约保函误判

✕ D: 把warranty deed当成优先顺位来源了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定登记法下谁是BFP，再立刻问后手是否被庇护规则带着走。

考场速记

记住一句：先看BFP，后看庇护规则。只要后手是从BFP那里拿权利，自己有没有通知常常就不再是致命点。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man decided to give his farm to his nephew. The man took a deed to his attorney and told the attorney to deliver the deed to the nephew upon the man's death. The man also told the attorney to return the deed to him if he asked. None of these instructions to the attorney were in writing, and the deed was not recorded. The man then e-mailed the nephew informing him of the arrangement.
Shortly thereafter, the nephew died testate. In his will, he devised the farm to his daughter. Several years later, the man died intestate, survived by two sons. The nephew's daughter immediately claimed ownership of the farm and demanded that the attorney deliver the deed to her.
Must the attorney deliver the deed to the nephew's daughter?

choices.A: No, because a gratuitous death escrow is void unless supported by a written contract.
choices.B: No, because the man never placed the deed beyond his control.
choices.C: Yes, because the death of the nephew rendered the gratuitous death escrow irrevocable by the man.
choices.D: Yes, because the deed to the nephew was legally delivered when the man took it to his attorney.

questions.explanation:
Deed delivered through death escrow
Did grantor deliver valid
deed to escrow agent?
No
Yes
Was agent instructed to transfer deed
to grantee upon grantor's death?
No
Yes
Did grantor give up right to
retrieve deed?
No
Yes
No delivery(invalid death escrow)
Effective delivery

A deed effectively transfers ownership of a landowner's (grantor's) real property to another (grantee) when it is delivered to, and accepted by, the grantee. To deliver a deed through a valid death escrow, the grantor must:

• give the deed to an escrow agent (eg, attorney) with instructions to transfer it to the grantee upon the grantor's death and

• relinquish the right to take back the deed (ie, by placing the deed beyond his/her control).

Here, the man attempted to deliver a deed to the farm through death escrow. Though he gave his attorney the deed with instructions to deliver it to the nephew upon the man's death, the man explicitly retained the right to have the deed returned to him if asked. Since the man never placed the deed beyond his control, the death escrow was invalid (no delivery). As a result, the nephew never acquired ownership of the farm and could not devise it to his daughter. And since she has no interest in the farm, the attorney need not deliver the deed to her.

(Choice A) Since most death escrows are gratuitous, a contract (written or oral) is not required. Instead, the death escrow was void because the man retained the right to take back the deed.

(Choice C) A gratuitous death escrow becomes irrevocable once the grantor delivers the deed—not when the grantee dies.

(Choice D) Delivery is presumed when a deed is given to the grantee directly. But when the deed is given to an escrow agent, there is no delivery unless the grantor relinquishes his/her right to recover it. And since the man retained the right to have the deed returned, giving it to his attorney (escrow agent) did not constitute delivery.

📌 Educational Objective

A deed is delivered through a valid death escrow when (1) the deed is given to an escrow agent with instructions to transfer it to the grantee upon the grantor's death, and (2) the grantor relinquishes the right to take back the deed.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子决定将他的农场赠与他的侄子。该男子将一份地契交给他的律师，并告知律师在他去世后将地契交付给侄子。该男子还告诉律师，如果他提出要求，就将地契返还给他。对律师的这些指示均非书面形式，且该地契未被登记。随后，该男子通过电子邮件将此安排告知了其侄子。

此后不久，该侄子立有遗嘱去世。在其遗嘱中，他将该农场遗赠给了他的女儿。几年后，该男子无遗嘱去世，身后留下两个儿子。侄子的女儿立即主张对该农场的所有权，并要求律师将地契交付给她。

律师必须将地契交付给侄子的女儿吗？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为无偿的死亡第三方保管除非有书面合同支持，否则无效。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该男子从未将地契置于其控制之外。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为侄子的死亡使得该男子不可撤销无偿的死亡第三方保管。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为当该男子将地契交给他的律师时，地契已合法交付给侄子。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Titles - Delivery and Recording of Deed

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：死亡托管交付（death escrow）里，出让人有没有把契据真正交给第三方并且放手，不能随时要回。

三秒认题路径：

交托管人 → 死后转交 → 能否收回 → 是否放手 → 有无交付

核心法律规则

这题只用抓住的规则

契据（deed）要真正完成交付，关键不是写没写信，也不是有没有录音，而是出让人是否把契据放到受托人手里后，自己还保不保留撤回权。

做死亡托管（death escrow）时，必须同时满足：一是把契据交给托管代理人（escrow agent），二是指示其在出让人死亡时转交，三是出让人已经放弃取回契据的权利。

如果出让人仍可随时要回契据，那就不是有效交付；对方以后死了，或再把财产写给别人，都救不回这个漏洞。

核心判例： 无须特定判例名，这题直接按死亡托管交付的传统规则判断：保留取回权 = 没有把契据置于自己控制之外。

思维导图

先看：契据有没有被真正交给托管代理人？
有再问：出让人有没有把契据放到自己控制之外？
有→ 有效交付，死后再转交才成立
无→ 没交付，死亡托管无效
无→ 没有托管交付，直接失败
本题卡死点：他明确说“你问我就还我”——这说明他没有放手。
结论→ 不能让侄子的女儿拿到契据，选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他已经把契据交给律师，还发邮件告诉侄子，应该算“差不多送出去了”。

但考试真正问的是：他有没有把契据真正放到自己控制之外；只要还能随时要回，就还没交付成功。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干最关键的可按要求取回契据，说明他没把契据置于自己控制之外，所以死亡托管无效，律师不必把契据交给侄子的女儿。

❌ 概念混淆 | 书面要件误判

✕ A: 误以为written contract才有效，其实这里坏在没放手，不是坏在没书面合同。

❌ 法律适用 | 误把死亡当成生效点

✕ C: 误把侄子死亡当成自动锁定交付，但出让人在那之前一直保留收回权。

❌ 事实误判 | 直接交付偷换

✕ D: 把given to the grantee偷换成直接交给受托人，直接交付推定根本没出现。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否终局式“放手”再看死后转交；只要保留取回权，后面一切安排都救不回来。

考场速记

记住一句：死亡托管（death escrow）不是“先放着、以后再说”，而是“交出去且收不回来”。

这题的速记就是：先交给第三人，再放弃取回权；少一个，契据就没真正交付。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An uncle owned a valuable tract of land. The uncle executed a document in the form of a warranty deed of land, which was regular in all respects except that the only language designating the grantees in each of the granting and habendum clauses was: "The leaders of all the Protestant churches in County A." The instrument was acknowledged as required by statute and promptly and properly recorded. The uncle told his lawyer, but no one else, that he had made the conveyance as he did because he abhorred sectarianism in the Protestant movement and because he thought that the leaders would devote the asset to lessening sectarianism.
The uncle died suddenly and unexpectedly a week later, leaving a will that bequeathed and devised his entire estate to his niece. After probate of the will became final and the administration on the uncle's estate was closed, the niece instituted an appropriate action to quiet title to the land and properly served as defendant each Protestant church situated in the county.
The only evidence introduced consisted of the chain of title under which the uncle held, the probated will, the recorded deed, the fact that no person knew about the deed except the uncle and his lawyer, and the conversation the uncle had with his lawyer described above.
In the action to quiet title, who will prevail and why?

choices.A: The defendants, because a deed is prima facie valid until rebutted.
choices.B: The defendants, because recording established prima facie delivery until rebutted.
choices.C: The niece, because the state of the evidence would not support a finding of delivery of the deed.
choices.D: The niece, because there is inadequate identification of grantees in the deed.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Deed requirements
RequirementsValidInvalid
Written & signed by grantor
  • Any written instrument signed by grantor
  • Oral (except permissible gift)
  • Signed only by grantee
Identifies grantor & grantee
  • Separate grantor & grantee (except concurrent estates)
  • Identifiable by name or description
  • Ambiguous/unidentifiable grantee(s)
  • Nonexistent grantee
Identifies land
  • Identifiable by reasonable certainty
  • eg:
  • Government survey
  • Metes & bounds
  • Street, lot, house number
  • Ambiguous description (but extrinsic evidence admissible)
  • Undefined part of larger parcel
Includes words of transfer
  • "Convey"
  • "Transfer"
  • "Grant"
  • "Sell"
  • "Lease"
  • "Rent"
  • "License"

A deed is a legal instrument that transfers ownership of real property from the grantor (old owner) to the grantee (new owner). To be valid, a deed must:

  • be in writing and signed by the grantor
  • unambiguously identify the grantor and grantee
  • unambiguously describe the land and
  • include words of transfer.

When a deed transfers ownership to a group of grantees, the identities of the group members must be ascertainable with reasonable certainty - eg, "the present members of the United States Congress." Extrinsic evidence can be used to clarify ambiguities. But if the extrinsic evidence is also unclear, a court will not speculate as to the grantor's intent and the deed will be deemed void (ie, of no legal effect).

Here, the uncle attempted to deed his land to "the leaders of all the Protestant churches in County A." But that description was ambiguous because there is no way to identify the specific individuals belonging to that group. And though the uncle's conversation with his lawyer (extrinsic evidence) was introduced, it did not resolve this ambiguity. Therefore, the inadequate identification of the grantees rendered the uncle's deed void. And since the deed did not convey title to the defendants, the niece will prevail in her action to quiet title.

(Choice A) A deed is not prima facie valid if it does not meet the above requirements. And since the deed here cannot satisfy all these requirements (due to the ambiguous description of the grantees), it is invalid.

(Choices B & C) A deed is valid if it meets the above requirements, and the transfer of the described land is effective when the deed is delivered and accepted. While recording is prima facie evidence that the deed was delivered to the grantee, it does not establish the deed's validity.

📌 Educational Objective

A valid deed (1) is in writing and signed by the grantor, (2) unambiguously identifies the grantor and grantee, (3) unambiguously describes the land, and (4) includes words of transfer. The identity of the parties and the land must be ascertainable with reasonable certainty, but extrinsic evidence can be used to resolve ambiguities.
questions.zh-question:
一位叔叔拥有一块有价值的土地。该叔叔签署了一份土地担保契据（warranty deed）形式的文件，该文件在所有方面均符合规范，唯一的例外是在授予条款（granting clause）和财产所有权条款（habendum clause）中，指定受让人的唯一语言是：“A县所有新教教会的领袖。”该文书已按法规要求进行公证，并及时、妥善地进行了登记。该叔叔告诉他的律师，但没有告诉其他人，他之所以这样做（进行转让），是因为他憎恶新教运动中的宗派主义，并认为这些领袖会利用该资产来减少宗派主义。

一周后，该叔叔突然意外去世，留下了一份遗嘱，将其全部遗产遗赠给他的侄女。在遗嘱认证终结且叔叔的遗产管理程序结束后，侄女提起了适当的确认土地所有权诉讼（action to quiet title），并将该县的每个新教教会作为被告并进行了妥善送达。

所提交的唯一证据包括叔叔持有的所有权链（chain of title）、经认证的遗嘱、已登记的契据、除叔叔及其律师外无人知晓该契据的事实，以及上文所述叔叔与律师的谈话。

在确认土地所有权诉讼中，谁将胜诉？为什么？

zh-choices.A: 被告，因为契据在被反驳前是初步有效的（prima facie valid）。
zh-choices.B: 被告，因为登记构成了初步的交付证据（prima facie delivery），直到被反驳为止。
zh-choices.C: 侄女，因为证据状况不足以支持契据已交付的裁定。
zh-choices.D: 侄女，因为契据中对受让人的身份识别不充分。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Titles - Delivery and Recording of Deed

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：契据（deed）里对受让人身份写得太模糊时，即使已经签字、录入和“交付”外观都在，仍可能因为受让人无法以合理确定性识别而无效。

三秒认题路径：

看受让人是谁 → 能否识别 → 不能识别就无效 → 录音不补救 → 选原告赢

核心法律规则

这题只要抓住四件事

契据（deed）要有效，必须书面、由出让人签字、明确写出出让人和受让人、并且能以合理确定性描述土地；受让人（grantee）如果写成一群无法辨认具体成员的人，考试上就会直接卡死。

这里的关键不是“有没有看起来像转让”，而是“法院能不能知道到底转给谁了”。Extrinsic evidence 可以帮你解释模糊，但不能把一个根本无法识别的受让人群体硬变成可识别对象。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用本题；本题锁定的是契据有效性规则：受让人不能以合理确定性识别时，契据无效，录音也救不回来。

思维导图

先问：这份文件是不是有效契据（deed）？
YES 书面、签字、土地能识别、受让人能识别、还有转让用语。
NO 受让人写成“County A 里所有 Protestant churches 的 leaders”，具体是谁根本抓不出来。
卡死点：不是“有没有录音”，而是“受让人能否以合理确定性识别”；这一步失败，契据无效。
误导点 recording（录音） 只能提示曾经交付过，不能替你补上无效受让人。
结论 契据不生效，土地仍留在出让人一方；遗嘱继承人来 quiet title，赢。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：契据已经签了、也登记了，而且还有律师证词，应该足以说明叔叔真想把地送出去。

但考试真正问的是：受让人到底能不能被法律上识别出来；只要“谁是受让人”这一步不清楚，后面的交付、登记、主观意图都救不了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的交代有没有发生」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的受让人名称无法确定具体成员，所以契据在最核心的一步就失败了；登记和律师转述都不能把一个无效受让人变成有效转让。

❌ 概念混淆 | 交付推定误判

✕ A: 把“看起来像契据”当成“已经有效”。

❌ 法律适用 | 登记补强误判

✕ B: 把 recording 当成有效性的替代品。

❌ 事实误判 | 交付争点偷换

✕ C: 只盯着交付，忽略“受让人是谁”根本没写清。

这题建议用什么方法？

先查契据有效性四要件，再看受让人能否以合理确定性识别；登记只是外观，不是修复无效条款的补丁。

考场速记

记住一句：deed 先看“谁收、收什么、怎么转”；只要受让人写到法院都认不出来，后面的登记和主观意图都不够。

口诀：“先认人，再认地；人认不出，契据先死。”

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A woman duly executed a will under which she devised her farm to her nephew and bequeathed the residue of her estate to her niece.
For 12 years after executing her will, the woman lived on her farm. Then she sold it and used the sale proceeds to purchase a home in the city, in which she lived until she died, never having changed her will.
Following the admission of the will to probate, both the nephew and the niece claimed ownership of the home. There is no applicable statute.
Who is the owner of the home?

choices.A: The nephew, because of the doctrine of ademption.
choices.B: The nephew, because of the doctrine of equitable estoppel.
choices.C: The niece, because of the doctrine of lapse.
choices.D: The niece, because she is the residuary legatee.

questions.explanation:
Classification of devises
(conveyance by will)

Type Definition Examples
Specific Devise of specifically identified asset • "my farm to my nephew"
General Devise (often of money) payable from general assets of estate • "$2,000 to my daughter"
• "one-half of my estate to my son"
Demonstrative Devise primarily payable from designated source, but secondarily payable from general assets • "$2,000 to my daughter out of my bank account"
Residuary Devise of all property not disposed of by specific, general, or demonstrative devise • "all of the remainder of my estate to my niece"

The woman (testator) specifically devised her farm to the nephew (devisee). She later sold that farm and used the proceeds to purchase a home. But the nephew is not entitled to that home because of the doctrine of ademption, which causes a devise to fail in two circumstances:

  • Ademption by extinction – when the specifically devised asset is not owned by the testator (or is destroyed or fundamentally changed) at the time of death (as seen here)
  • Ademption by satisfaction – when the devisee received the devised asset (or some other asset intended to satisfy the devise) during the testator's life (not applicable here)

As a result, the devise takes nothing unless the will expressly states otherwise. So, when a specifically devised asset (eg, the farm) is sold during the testator's lifetime, the sale proceeds—and any assets later acquired with those proceeds (eg, the home)—become part of the general estate. The general estate is then distributed in accordance with the remainder of the will. And since the woman's will bequeathed the residue of her estate to the niece, the niece owns the home as the residuary legatee ((Choice D)).

(Choice B) The doctrine of equitable estoppel bars a party from asserting a material fact that is inconsistent with a prior representation upon which another party detrimentally relied. But this doctrine does not apply here since no party has asserted contradictory facts.

(Choice C) The doctrine of lapse causes any type of devise to fail when the devisee dies before the testator. But since the nephew and niece (devisees) survived the woman (testator), neither devise will fail under this doctrine.

📌 Educational Objective

Specific devises are deemed by extinction when the devised asset is not owned by the testator (or is destroyed or fundamentally changed) upon death. And any type of devise is deemed by satisfaction when the devised asset or a substituted asset is given during the testator's life. The devised asset will then join the general estate.

📚 References
  • 80 Am. Jur. 2d Wills § 1444 (2018) (doctrine of ademption).
questions.zh-question:
一名女士妥善订立了一份遗嘱，根据该遗嘱，她将其农场遗赠给她的侄子，并将其剩余遗产遗赠给她的侄女。

订立遗嘱后的12年里，该女士一直住在她的农场。然后她卖掉了农场，并用出售所得在城里购买了一套房子，她一直住在那里直到去世，期间从未更改过遗嘱。

遗嘱被提交进行遗嘱认证后，侄子和侄女都声称拥有这套房子的所有权。本案没有适用的成文法。

谁是这套房子的所有权人？

zh-choices.A: 侄子，因为“遗赠标的物不存在”(ademption)原则。
zh-choices.B: 侄子，因为“衡平法上的禁止反言”(equitable estoppel)原则。
zh-choices.C: 侄女，因为“遗赠失效”(lapse)原则。
zh-choices.D: 侄女，因为她是剩余遗产的受遗赠人。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Titles - Titles

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：特定遗赠的农场被卖掉后，房子不是给受遗赠人，而是落回遗嘱剩余财产，最后归残余受遗赠人。

三秒认题路径：

特定遗赠 → 生前卖掉 → 代物买房 → 特定遗赠失效 → 残余受遗赠人拿走

核心法律规则

特定遗赠（specific devise）是指把某一项被点名的财产直接送给某人，考场意思：这份礼物盯的是“那一块东西”本身。若该财产在立遗嘱人死亡时已经不在遗产里，或被实质改变，就发生 遗赠消灭（ademption by extinction），考场意思：这份礼物直接失效。

这里农场先被卖掉，卖价又拿去买了新房，所以原来的特定遗赠不会自动“跟着钱走”给侄子；除非遗嘱特别说要保留替代物，否则这笔新房进入一般遗产，按剩余条款分配。

残余受遗赠（residuary devise）拿走的是“其他人都没拿到的剩下部分”，考场意思：前面那份特定礼物一失效，剩下的新房就掉进残余池里。

核心判例： 无需具体判例名；本题直接用 ademption by extinction 锁定：特定遗赠财产在死亡时已不在，故失效，残余受遗赠人取走房屋。

思维导图

先看遗嘱送的是不是“点名财产”？
是： 农场是 特定遗赠（specific devise），不是金额型赠与。
再看： 死亡时农场还在不在？
不在：农场已卖掉，触发 ademption by extinction，侄子拿不到替代房。
结果： 卖地所得与后买的房进一般遗产；遗嘱剩余条款把“剩下的”留给侄女。
结论： 房屋归 残余受遗赠人（residuary legatee），也就是侄女。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然农场卖了，钱又买成了房子，那侄子应该“接着拿”新房。

但考试真正问的是：特定遗赠的标的是否还存在；不是看替代物是不是“感觉上同一笔钱”。 这题里房子不是自动回给侄子，而是回到遗产剩余部分。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的农场已被卖掉且遗嘱未改，特定遗赠先失效，房屋进入剩余遗产，所以最后归侄女。

❌ 法律适用 | 消灭对象错认

✕ A: 把ademption用反了，侄子不是拿房，而是失去这份特定礼物。

❌ 概念混淆 | 衡平法张冠李戴

✕ B: 题干没谁前后矛盾地作出承诺，equitable estoppel根本没戏。

❌ 事实误判 | 先死条件偷换

✕ C: lapse要的是受遗赠人先于立遗嘱人死亡，但两人都活到了继承开始。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯遗赠类型，再查死亡时标的是否还在；看到“卖掉再买房”，先想消灭，不要先想替代继承。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“特定财产不在了，特定遗赠就没了；剩余财产最后归残余受遗赠人。”

本题还可顺手记：ademption看“标的还在不在”，lapse看“受遗赠人先没先死”。

reason.zh: 设立特定遗赠；若死亡时不再拥有该农场则可能失效。

reason.zh: 特定遗赠失效后售款及购置房产归入剩余遗产由其取得。

highlights.text: devised her farm to her nephew and bequeathed the residue of her estate to her niece

label.zh: 特定遗赠与剩余遗产遗赠

reason.en: Sets up the classification that determines where the home passes after ademption.
reason.zh: 确立遗赠分类，决定特定遗赠失效后房产归属。

highlights.text: sold it and used the sale proceeds to purchase a home in the city

reason.en: The sale eliminates the specific devise and channels value into the general estate.
reason.zh: 出售使特定遗赠消灭，价值转入一般遗产。

highlights.text: never having changed her will

label.zh: 无反特定遗赠失效条款

reason.zh: 遗嘱未变更，无明示条款保留侄儿对替代财产的请求权。

highlights.text: both the nephew and the niece claimed ownership of the home

reason.zh: 问题核心在于失效的农场遗赠还是剩余条款支配城市住宅。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A woman who owned a house executed a deed purporting to convey the house to her son and his wife. The language of the deed was sufficient to create a common law joint tenancy with right of survivorship, which is unmodified by statute in the jurisdiction. The woman mailed the deed to the son with a letter saying: "Because I intend you and your wife to have my house after my death, I am enclosing a deed to the house. However, I intend to live in the house for the rest of my life, so don't record the deed until I die. The deed will be effective at my death."
The son put the deed in his desk. The wife discovered the deed and recorded it without the son's knowledge. Subsequently, the son and the wife separated, and the wife, without telling anyone, conveyed her interest in the house to a friend who immediately reconveyed it to the wife.
The woman learned that the son and the wife had separated and also learned what had happened to the deed to the house. The woman then brought an appropriate action against the son and the wife to obtain a declaration that the woman was still the owner of the house and an order canceling of record the woman's deed and the subsequent deeds.
If the court determines that the woman owns the house in fee simple, what will be the likely explanation?

choices.A: The deed was not delivered.
choices.B: The wife's conduct entitles the woman to equitable relief.
choices.C: The woman expressly reserved a life estate.
choices.D: The woman received no consideration for her deed.

questions.explanation:
Presumed delivery of deed
  • Physical delivery (eg, by hand or mail)
  • Recording
  • Unconditional delivery to agent
  • Grantee obtains possession of deed

A deed is a legal instrument that transfers an interest in real property from the owner (grantor) to another (grantee) once it has been:

• delivered — evidenced by the grantor's intent to presently transfer an interest to the grantee, even if the interest itself is a future interest (ie, the possessory rights transfer later) and

• accepted — presumed if the transfer benefits the grantee.

Recording a deed (ie, depositing it in official land records) creates a presumption of delivery. But this presumption can be rebutted by evidence that the grantor did not intend to presently transfer an interest to the grantee—eg, if the transfer was contingent upon a future event.

Here, delivery is presumed since the wife recorded the deed. But that presumption can be rebutted since the woman mailed the deed with a letter explaining that she only wanted the son and wife to have her house after her death (transfer contingent upon future event). Therefore, the court will likely determine that the woman owns the house in fee simple because the deed was not delivered.

(Choice B) A court may grant an injured party equitable relief (eg, rescinding or reforming a deed) to prevent unjust enrichment of a wrongdoer when other remedies are insufficient. Here, the wife was likely a wrongdoer since she recorded and conveyed the deed without the son's knowledge. But the court can hold that the woman owns the property since the deed was not delivered (sufficient remedy), so equitable relief is not needed.

(Choice C) A life estate is a possessory interest in land that is limited in duration by a life (eg, "To A for life"). Here, the woman attempted to reserve a life estate in her letter—not in the deed. But had she reserved a life estate in the deed, she would not own the home in fee simple since her ownership interest would terminate upon her death.

(Choice D) Consideration (eg, monetary payment) is not needed to create a valid deed or to effectively transfer a property interest to another.

📌 Educational Objective

To transfer an interest in real property, a deed must be delivered (and accepted). Delivery occurs when the grantor intends to presently transfer an interest to the grantee. Therefore, delivery is ineffective if the transfer is contingent upon a future event.
questions.zh-question:
一位拥有一所房屋的女性签署了一份地契，意图将其房屋转让给她的儿子和儿媳。该地契的语言足以根据普通法创立具有遗属权的共同共有关系（common law joint tenancy with right of survivorship），且该司法管辖区的成文法并未对此进行修改。这位女性将地契邮寄给儿子，并附上一封信，信中说：“因为我打算在我去世后让你们夫妻拥有我的房子，所以我附上这份房子的地契。但是，我打算在这所房子里度过我的余生，所以在我去世前不要登记这份地契。这份地契将在我去世时生效。”

儿子将地契放在他的书桌里。儿媳发现了这份地契，并在儿子不知情的情况下进行了登记。随后，儿子和儿媳分居，儿媳在没有告知任何人的情况下，将其在房屋中的权益转让给一位朋友，该朋友立即又将该权益转回给了儿媳。

这位女性得知儿子和儿媳已经分居，也知道了房屋地契所发生的事情。于是，这位女性对儿子和儿媳提起了适当的诉讼，请求法院宣告她仍然是房屋的所有人，并下令撤销她那份地契以及后续地契的登记记录。

如果法院最终裁定该女性以完全所有权（fee simple）拥有该房屋，最可能的解释是什么？

zh-choices.A: 地契未被交付。
zh-choices.B: 儿媳的行为使该女性有权获得衡平法上的救济。
zh-choices.C: 该女性明确保留了终身地产权（life estate）。
zh-choices.D: 该女性的地契没有收到对价。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Titles - Titles

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：契据交付（delivery of deed）是否成立；只要赠与人只是想“死后再生效”，这份契据就还没真正交付，受让人拿到地契也不算数。

三秒认题路径：

有契据 → 先看交付 → 看现在转移意图 → 只是死后生效 → 未交付

核心法律规则

不动产里的契据（deed）要有效转让，必须先交付（delivery），再接受（acceptance）。这里的交付，考场意思是：赠与人必须打算presently transfer，也就是现在就把权益推出去，不是等未来某个事件发生才算数。

把契据邮寄（mailing）或登记（recording），通常会推定已经交付；但如果题干证明赠与人只想让对方“after my death”才拿到房子，这个推定就会被推翻。

核心判例：Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用本题；本题的锁定规则是：契据登记只是推定交付，但死后才生效的条件会把推定打掉。

思维导图

先问：这份契据有没有真正交付（delivery）？
线索1：契据被邮件寄出、后来又被登记（recorded） → 先有“已交付”的推定。
线索2：但信里写的是“after my death”才给你们房子 → 这不是现在转移。
第二关：赠与人当时是不是想presently transfer？
如果是：交付成立，产权可能已经出去。
如果否：只是把纸先放出去，法律上还没送出房产。
卡死点：本题明确写明“effective at my death” → 条件挂在未来事件上 → 未交付。
结论：法院会认定原主仍是fee simple 持有人，所以选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：契据都被登记了，怎么还说没过户？

但考试真正问的是：赠与人当时有没有把房子现在就交出去，而不是先把纸交出去、等自己死后再生效。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的纸有没有离开手」。这里最致命的不是登记动作，而是信里把生效时间推到未来，直接推翻交付推定。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里最关键的 “effective at my death” 说明她只想死后才转移权益，所以即使后来被登记，交付（delivery）仍未成立。

❌ 法律适用 | 衡平救济误判

✕ B: 盯着妻子私自登记就想上 equitable relief，但本题先用交付规则就能解决。

❌ 概念混淆 | 寿命地产误判

✕ C: 把信里的“住到死”当成 life estate，但保留条件不在契据里。

❌ 事实误判 | 价金条件偷换

✕ D: 以为没给钱就没转让，其实 consideration 不是有效契据的门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“现在转移意图”，再看登记推定能不能被“死后生效”这句话打掉。

考场速记

记住：契据交付看的是“现在给不给”，不是“纸先不先到”。如果题干写了死后才生效、未来事件才生效，通常就是未交付。

口诀：先看delivery，再看acceptance；recording 只会帮你推定，不会替你补出“现在转移”的意思。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
Under the terms of his duly probated will, a testator devised his house to his "grandchildren in fee simple" and the residue of his estate to his brother. The testator had had two children, a son and a daughter, but only the daughter survived him. At the time of the testator's death, the daughter was 30 years old and had two minor children (grandchildren of the testator) who also survived the testator.
A third grandchild of the testator, who was the child of the testator's predeceased son, had been alive when the testator executed the will, but he had predeceased the testator. Under the applicable intestate succession laws, the deceased grandchild's sole heir was his mother.
A statute of the jurisdiction provides as follows: "If a devisee, including a devisee of a class gift, who is a grandparent or a lineal descendant of a grandparent of the testator is dead at the time of execution of the will or fails to survive the testator, the issue of such deceased devisee shall take the deceased's share under the will, unless the will expressly provides that this statute shall not apply. For this purpose, words of survivorship, such as 'if he survives me,' are a sufficient expression that the statute shall not apply."
Who now owns the house?

choices.A: The testator's brother.
choices.B: The testator's two surviving grandchildren.
choices.C: The testator's two surviving grandchildren and all other grandchildren who are born to the testator's daughter.
choices.D: The testator's two surviving grandchildren and the deceased grandchild's mother.

questions.explanation:
Devise of class gift

A gift is a voluntary transfer of property without payment or consideration (eg, by devise). A class gift is created when the gift recipients (ie, donees) are unspecified but can be identified in the future (eg, upon the donor's death). Under the rule of convenience, a class closes once any member is entitled to immediate possession of the property, and anyone born after the class closes cannot claim an interest in that property.*

However, if a donee receives a gift under a will and predeceases the testator, the gift will lapse and become invalid unless the will or a statute provides otherwise. An anti-lapse statute (as seen here) will save the gift from lapsing if the donee has a specified family relation to the testator AND the donee is survived by his/her own children or other lineal descendants (ie, issue). The surviving issue will then take the gift in place of the donee.

Here, the testator devised his house to his "grandchildren in fee simple." The testator had three grandchildren, one of whom predeceased the testator. This jurisdiction's anti-lapse statute applies to a testator's lineal descendants. But it does not save the deceased grandchild's gift because his sole heir was his mother-ie, he has no lineal descendants. As a result, the house is now owned by the testator's two surviving grandchildren (Choices C & D).

*Those born after a class closes are excluded from the class, but those already in utero upon closing are included.

(Choice A) The brother, as the recipient of the residuary estate, would have received the house had no grandchildren been eligible for the devise (eg, had they all predeceased the testator without lineal descendants).

📌 Educational Objective

A gift conveyed under a will typically lapses if the recipient predeceases the testator. However, an anti-lapse statute will save the gift if the recipient (1) has a specified family relation to the testator and (2) is survived by his/her children or other lineal descendants.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Wills and Other Donative Transfers §§ 1.2, 5.5 (Am. Law Inst. 1999) (lapse and anti-lapse statutes).
questions.zh-question:
根据其经正式遗嘱认证的遗嘱条款，一名立遗嘱人将其房屋“以完全保有地产权的形式”遗赠给其“孙子女”，并将其剩余遗产遗赠给其兄弟。该立遗嘱人曾有两个子女，一个儿子和一个女儿，但只有女儿在其去世时仍在世。在立遗嘱人去世时，其女儿30岁，并有两个未成年的子女（即立遗嘱人的孙子女），他们也都在立遗嘱人去世时在世。

立遗嘱人的第三个孙子女，是其先于自己去世的儿子的孩子，在立遗嘱人订立遗嘱时在世，但先于立遗嘱人去世。根据适用的无遗嘱继承法，该已故孙子女的唯一继承人是其母亲。

该司法管辖区的一项法规规定如下：“如果一名受遗赠人（包括类组赠与中的受遗赠人），其是立遗嘱人的祖父母或祖父母的直系后代，在遗嘱订立时已死亡或未能于立遗嘱人去世时存活，则该已故受遗赠人的子嗣应继承该已故者的份额，除非遗嘱明确规定本法规不适用。为此目的，表示存续条件的词语，例如‘如果他比我晚去世’，即构成本法规不适用的充分表示。”

现在谁拥有这栋房屋的所有权？

zh-choices.A: 立遗嘱人的兄弟。
zh-choices.B: 立遗嘱人的两名在世孙子女。
zh-choices.C: 立遗嘱人的两名在世孙子女，以及其女儿日后所生的所有其他孙子女。
zh-choices.D: 立遗嘱人的两名在世孙子女和已故孙子女的母亲。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Titles - Future interests

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：遗嘱里的类赠与（class gift）里，先死掉的孙辈会不会被反失效法（anti-lapse statute）救回来；答案是看他有没有能代位的直系后代（issue），没有就失效。

三秒认题路径：

类赠与 → 先死亡 → 查反失效 → 有无后代 → 只剩存活孙辈

核心法律规则

遗嘱赠与如果受赠人先于立遗嘱人死亡，通常会失效（lapse）；考试上先别急着找“谁更像家人”，先看有没有适用反失效法（anti-lapse statute）。

这里的关键是：受赠人必须是法条点名的亲属，而且还得有自己的直系后代（issue），这样才由后代代位拿到那一份。若没有后代，法条救不了，那个份额就回到类赠与剩余成员或按遗嘱其他安排走。

核心判例： 这题对应的是类赠与与反失效法的经典规则：“先死的成员若无可代位后代，就不会把份额带进来。”

思维导图

先看：这是不是“能立刻上诉/程序性命令”那类题？
不是。 本题是类赠与（class gift）里先死成员的份额怎么处理。
第一关： 先死的孙辈是否属于法条保护的亲属？
是，但还不够：还要看他有没有自己的直系后代。
第二关： 他有没有 surviving issue？
没有。题干说他死后只有母亲是法定继承人，说明他没有自己的直系后代。
结论： 反失效法不救这一份，类赠与只剩下活着的两名孙辈分房子。
答案： 选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然先死的那个孙辈也是“grandchild”，那他的份额应该自动进到母亲手里，或者把房子分给所有将来出生的孙辈。

但考试真正问的是：这个人有没有自己的直系后代可以代位拿份额。没有的话，反失效法救不了他；而且类赠与一旦在可立即占有时关闭，后面才出生的人通常进不来。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 先死的孙辈没有自己的直系后代，所以反失效法救不了他的那一份，房子只落到两个仍存活的孙辈手里。

❌ 事实误判 | 残余财产误认

✕ A: 把 residuary estate 误当兜底分房子，题干里类赠与没全灭。

❌ 法律适用 | 未来出生误套

✕ C: 以为还会扩到 born to 的后代，但类赠与已在可领取时关闭。

❌ 概念混淆 | 代位继承混用

✕ D: 把 mother 当成能代位的人，但她不是这份遗嘱下的直系后代。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定类赠与，再问先死者有没有自己的后代；没有后代，就别让反失效法硬救。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“先死看反失效，有后代才代位；没后代就失效，类赠与关门时看现存成员。”

看到遗嘱类赠与，先问“有没有 surviving issue”，再决定份额是由后代接手，还是直接落回仍存活的类成员。

reason.en: Creates a class gift to the testator's grandchildren rather than named individuals.
reason.zh: 创设对孙辈的类别赠与，而非指名个人。

reason.zh: 已故孙辈仅有旁系继承人，反失效法规不适用。

highlights.text: issue of such deceased devisee shall take the deceased's share under the will

reason.en: The statute saves a lapsed share only for the deceased devisee's lineal descendants.
reason.zh: 法规仅在已故受遗赠人有直系卑亲属时挽救失效份额。
